reviews.evidence: The file is a navigation section: its headings and linked entries organize the subject but define no mathematical object, so an empty prerequisite list is correct.

The core requires a symplectic manifold, a completely integrable Hamiltonian system, Hamilton equations for the displayed motion, a diffeomorphism to B×T^n, and Lagrangian invariant tori. The Liouville–Arnold theorem and regular fibers occur only in the existence section, so they are not prerequisites.

The core constructs C∞(M) from the smooth manifold M and pointwise function operations. The C∞-ring, smooth-map pullback, algebra-homomorphism, vector-bundle modules, and bump-function links appear as later structure or examples; adding them would make derived material prerequisite to the basic algebra.

The definition needs smooth maps between smooth manifolds and almost-complex structures to state df∘J_M=J_N∘df. Integrability and holomorphic maps are explicitly deferred to the final paragraph, so they are not defining inputs.

The core is a smooth endomorphism of the tangent bundle over a smooth manifold with J²=−id; tangent-space and vector-bundle foundations supply the pointwise and bundle data. Complex manifolds, integrability, maps, and symplectic manifolds are later comparisons.

The triple consists of a smooth manifold, an almost-complex structure, and a compatible Hermitian/Riemannian metric on (TM,J). The fundamental form and symplectic, integrable, and Kähler conditions are consequences or stronger variants.

The defining datum is a rank-three subbundle Q⊂End_R(TM) with local quaternion frames over a smooth manifold. An almost-complex structure and quaternionic vector-bundle structure are explicitly identified as insufficient or stronger near-misses, so they were removed; vector-bundle supplies the bundle foundation.

The definition requires a smooth manifold, a smooth 2-form, tangent spaces, and pointwise nondegeneracy modeled by symplectic vector spaces. Closedness and the resulting symplectic manifold, bundle map, and vector field are later consequences.

The core requires a smooth manifold, diffeomorphism-valued time slices, embedded submanifolds for the subset application, smooth isotopy context, and the smooth map N×[0,1]→N in the manifold-with-boundary sense. The diffeomorphism-group and vector-field links occur only in the convention/example sections.

The definition requires a C¹ flow on a compact manifold, its tangent-bundle splitting into vector subbundles, the differential of the flow, and a norm for exponential estimates. The geodesic-flow example is downstream and not a prerequisite.

The theorem starts with a quadratic form and Clifford algebra and identifies its filtration’s associated graded algebra with the exterior algebra. The principal-symbol link is explanatory notation in the proof idea, not an additional defining hypothesis.

The hypotheses and conclusion require a Hamiltonian torus action on a compact connected symplectic manifold, a moment map, convex hull, and connected components for fixed sets. The moment polytope and nonabelian/noncompact variants are consequences and scope limits.

The core is a bijective holomorphic map between complex manifolds whose inverse is holomorphic; complex manifolds and holomorphic maps are therefore direct inputs. The category, diffeomorphism, exponential-map example, and local criterion are later context.

The group is defined as biholomorphisms of a complex manifold, interpreted as automorphisms in the category of complex manifolds. Topologies and Lie-group structure are explicitly optional later additions.

The group is formed from bordism-equivalence classes of closed manifolds under disjoint union, with the abelian-group laws checked afterward. The chosen tangential structure is part of the stated bordism theory rather than an unmentioned universal prerequisite.

Boundary and interior are defined from the half-space chart condition on a manifold with boundary. The induced boundary smooth structure, diffeomorphism invariance, and ambient-boundary contrast are consequences.

A boundary chart is a smooth-atlas chart from a manifold with boundary to a relatively open subset of the Euclidean half-space, with smooth extensions of transitions. Subspace topology and ordinary smooth charts are explanatory foundations already represented by the atlas/manifold inputs.

The definition is a nonnegative smooth function on a manifold with boundary whose zero set is the boundary and for which 0 is a regular value. Boundary charts and collars are used only for the later normal-form/existence discussion.

A boundary face is a connected component of the abstract boundary of a manifold with corners. The connected-component target is direct; corner stratification and incidence at corners are later consequences.
The orientation is induced on the boundary of an oriented manifold with boundary by the outward-normal-first rule. Stokes’ theorem is an application in a later section, so it is not a prerequisite.

The core defines a bump function as a smooth map whose support is compact; the smooth-manifold, smooth-map, and compact-set targets supply exactly those data. Closed sets and neighborhoods occur only in the optional localized variant, so those edges were removed.

The axioms quantify over smooth maps between finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, with projections, composition, and nullary constants. Euclidean space is the direct setting; the smooth-function algebra is introduced only as a later example.

The selected convention defines the object as a connected compact Kähler manifold with holomorphically trivial canonical bundle. Metrics, Kähler classes, holomorphic-symplectic examples, and the Calabi–Yau theorem are later consequences or examples.

The theorem explicitly assumes a compact Kähler manifold and Kähler class and concludes a Kähler form with prescribed Ricci form; the Kähler form, Ricci form, and metric targets are direct inputs to the displayed formulation. Hyperkähler and full curvature links are scope remarks.

The core constructs the top exterior power of the holomorphic cotangent bundle and identifies it as a holomorphic line bundle over a complex manifold. The three listed targets are therefore the direct construction inputs; sections and trivializations are later.

The proof uses a smooth action, its cotangent lift, the equivariant moment-map condition, and Hamiltonian Lie-group-action terminology. The moment-map link in the coordinate example is an output/application and need not be an additional edge.

The definition applies the exterior derivative to the tautological one-form on a cotangent bundle over a smooth manifold. Closedness and nondegeneracy establish symplecticity afterward; cotangent naturality and Hamiltonian signs are later applications.

The objects and morphisms are complex manifolds and holomorphic maps, while category/core foundations justify identities, composition, and the maximal subgroupoid. Biholomorphisms and the underlying smooth category are later comparisons.

The objects and morphisms are symplectic manifolds and pullback-preserving symplectic maps. Category/core foundations justify composition and isomorphisms; immersions, symplectomorphisms, and the subgroupoid are consequences.

The core uses the timelike-curve convention retained here. Checked against the cited Geroch and Bär–Ginoux–Pfäffle treatments, which define a Cauchy hypersurface by meeting every inextendible timelike curve exactly once; global hyperbolicity is treated as the later characterization. The causal-curve prerequisite remains useful for the corpus definition of causal/timelike curves.

The core uses the Lorentzian metric and time orientation to define future/past nonspacelike curves. The timelike clause was corrected to require a nonzero tangent, preventing a constant curve from being timelike by vacuity. Integration classification: the reviewed current source includes a repair relative to the preceding validated commit.

The object is exactly J⁺(p)∩J⁻(q), requiring the Lorentzian setting and causal-future/past definitions. Global hyperbolicity is introduced only as a condition involving compact diamonds and strong causality.
The construction starts with the future null cone in Minkowski space and quotients by positive rays. The S² and CP¹ identifications and Lorentz/Möbius interpretations are subsequent descriptions.

The distribution is the symplectic orthogonal of tangent spaces to a coisotropic submanifold and is asserted to be a vector subbundle. Foliation, involutivity, Hamiltonian examples, and reduction follow later.

The foliation integrates the characteristic distribution on a coisotropic submanifold of a symplectic manifold. Frobenius, Lie brackets, Hamiltonian examples, and quotient reduction are explanatory consequences.

The operator is the normalized Clifford volume element acting on an even-dimensional spinor module, with Clifford anticommutation and half-spin eigenspaces. Gamma matrices occur only in the later matrix-realization paragraph, so that edge was removed.
The definitions of I± and J± use a time-oriented Lorentzian manifold and causal/timelike curves. Causal diamonds are a later intersection of these sets, not an input.

The core packages a symplectic manifold with a Hamiltonian function and its uniquely determined vector field. Cotangent models, Hamiltonian flow/system, Poisson structures, and constrained mechanics are later applications.

Clean intersection requires embedded submanifolds of a smooth manifold and the tangent equality T_p(S∩T)=T_pS∩T_pT. Transversality and connected-component material occurs in later comparison/examples.

The quotient requires a module over a commutative ring with 2 invertible, a quadratic form, and the tensor algebra. Inner products, universal properties, Clifford modules, and associated graded results are later specializations or consequences.

The theorem builds the Lie superalgebra bracket from the polarization b_q of q and then identifies its central quotient with Cl(V,q); the two supergeometry targets and quadratic-form target are direct inputs.

The definition is a module together with a unital homomorphism from a Clifford algebra, equivalently a linear Clifford multiplication map. Module, algebra-homomorphism, and linear-map targets are used in the core; graded/super and spinor material is later.

The orbit is formed from a Lie group, Lie algebra, coadjoint action, orbit, and stabilizer. The core also explicitly equips G/G_lambda→O_lambda with a diffeomorphism, so the diffeomorphism prerequisite is direct; the symplectic/KKS structure is later.

The core requires closed boundary manifolds, a compact manifold with boundary, and an identification ∂W≅M0⊔M1. Diffeomorphism and disjoint-union targets were added for that boundary data; equivalence-relation language appears only in later convention material.

The category has closed manifolds as objects, cobordisms with collars as morphisms, and composition by gluing. Category, morphism, identity, cobordism, and collar-neighborhood foundations are all used by the core construction.

The relation is defined by existence of a cobordism between closed structured manifolds; the equivalence-relation target and cobordism/closed-manifold targets are used directly, while collar gluing is the proof of transitivity.

The codifferential is the formal adjoint of the exterior derivative on forms over an oriented Riemannian manifold, with the Hodge-star formula. Riemannian manifold, formal adjoint, exterior derivative, and Hodge star are all used in the core; Laplacian and integration-by-parts issues are later.

The theorem assumes a coisotropic submanifold whose characteristic foliation has a smooth leaf-space quotient and concludes the descended symplectic form. Coisotropic submanifold, characteristic foliation, smooth manifold, and symplectic manifold are the direct hypotheses/conclusion data.

The definition imposes (T_pC)^ω⊂T_pC for an embedded submanifold of a symplectic manifold. Symplectic manifold, embedded submanifold, coisotropic subspace, and smooth embedding provide the ambient and pointwise inputs; characteristic reduction is later.

The core defines W^ω⊂W inside a symplectic vector space and immediately constructs the quotient form. Symplectic vector space, linear subspace, and symplectic orthogonal complement are direct inputs; global reduction and related subspaces are later.

The theorem constructs a smooth embedding of ∂M×[0,1) into a manifold with boundary and identifies it diffeomorphically with an open neighborhood. Manifold-with-boundary, smooth embedding, product manifold, and boundary-smooth-map notions are direct.

The definition is a linear assignment from the Lie algebra to smooth functions satisfying the moment-map differential identity and Poisson bracket condition. Symplectic action, Lie algebra, linear map/homomorphism, Poisson algebra, infinitesimal generator, and vector field are all used in the core.

The complex restricts the de Rham differential to compactly supported forms and takes its cohomology. Smooth manifold, exterior derivative, compactly supported form, and de Rham complex are direct; proper pullback and duality are later.

The definition takes the compact support of a differential form on a smooth manifold and records the resulting vector space. Smooth manifold, differential k-form, compact set, and vector-space foundations are direct; integration and cohomology are later.
The compatible almost-complex source was outside this batch and remains triaged.

The core requires a Hamiltonian system and an involutive family of n functions, with functional independence on an open dense set. Regular values, action-angle coordinates, and Hamiltonian vector fields occur in later theorem/example sections.

A complex atlas is a covering family of complex-coordinate charts with holomorphic transitions, modulo the stated equivalence relation. The four listed targets supply the chart, manifold, transition-map, and equivalence data; complex-manifold is a later result.

The theorem assumes a finite-dimensional complex vector space with nondegenerate quadratic form and classifies its Clifford algebra modules. Quadratic form, Clifford algebra, and Clifford module are the direct theorem inputs; spin-group restriction is later.

The chart is a homeomorphism from an open subset of a topological manifold to an open subset of C^n. Topological-manifold and homeomorphism foundations are exactly the core data; holomorphic compatibility is deferred to atlases.

The definition uses a topological manifold with a compatible complex atlas and the underlying smooth-manifold structure. Holomorphic-map links occur in the transition condition and later morphism discussion, but adding holomorphic-map as a prerequisite would create the complex-manifold/holomorphic-map definition cycle.
The theorem identifies de Rham cohomology with real singular cohomology via integration; the four listed foundations are direct theorem data, while naturality and proof tools are later.
The definition counts orientation signs over a regular fiber of a proper smooth map; orientation, properness, and regular value are direct, while integration is later.
The operator is defined by conjugating Dolbeault with J on a hypercomplex manifold; that structure is the direct input and applications are later.
Depth counts vanishing boundary coordinates in a corner chart; manifold-with-corners is the sole direct input.
The criterion compares map transversality with product transversality to the embedded diagonal; all five listed notions occur in the theorem statement.
The definition uses smooth manifolds, diffeomorphisms, groupoids, cores, and the smooth-manifold category directly.
A flow is a C1 map from the real line times a smooth manifold satisfying composition laws; all four listed foundations are direct definition data.
A (p,q)-form is a smooth section of the type-decomposed complexified cotangent bundle; manifold, splitting, section, and wedge are direct.
The definition gives a linear differential operator between vector-bundle sections over a smooth manifold; the three listed foundations are direct.
A Dirac spinor uses a spinor module and immediately defines the associated spinor-bundle field; both are direct representations, with chirality later.
The construction uses component smooth manifolds and atlas, smooth embeddings, and the coproduct property in the smooth-manifold category directly.
Dolbeault cohomology is cohomology of the Dolbeault complex and a complex vector space; those four foundations are direct.
The complex consists of vector spaces of forms with Dolbeault differential; complex manifold, cochain complex, vector space, and operators are direct.
The operators are bidegree components of exterior derivative on a complex manifold; the three listed foundations are direct.
The double glues two boundary manifolds using a collar to produce a smooth manifold; all three listed foundations are direct.
The definition is Ricci equal to a scalar multiple of the metric on a Riemannian manifold; both listed foundations are direct.
Ellipticity is invertibility of the principal symbol of a differential operator between vector bundles; all four listed foundations are direct.
An equivariant moment map intertwines a Lie-group moment map with the coadjoint action; all three listed foundations are direct.
The definition is a symplectic manifold whose form is exact; both listed foundations are direct.
Fineness uses sheaves of abelian groups, open covers, and stalk support on a topological space; all five listed foundations are direct.

Criticality is failure of surjectivity of the differential and rank; matrix/Jacobian discussion is later explanatory material.
